scope: Lorentzian and Euclidean gauge-chiral superspace action, covariant D-algebra matter-density reduction, Wess-Zumino projections, component reductions, Wick continuation, and Euclidean contour

checks.locked: R labels L or E; mu labels 0 through 3; m labels 1 through 4; a and dot a are Weyl indices; I,J are matter indices; A,B are adjoint indices
c_AB^C denotes real Lie-algebra structure constants; f_AB(Phi) denotes the symmetric holomorphic gauge-kinetic matrix
mathcal V is the bridge exponent and mathcal E=exp(mathcal V) is the bridge; no undeclared exp(2V) normalization occurs

D and barD are Step-2A flat derivatives; nabla is the chiral-frame column derivative; the antichiral-frame row derivative and the chiral-frame right-module derivative nabla-left-arrow are separately defined and never conflated

F^I and tildeF_I are chiral auxiliaries; F_MN is gauge curvature; mathscr D^A is the vector auxiliary and mathcal D_M is the ordinary gauge-covariant derivative
mathscr U denotes the superpotential; mathcal W_a denotes the gauge field-strength superfield
D^2 and barD^2 index order is explicit; barD^2 acts first in the D-projector; all vertical-bar projections are ordered
mathscr D=+1/2 barD^dot a tildeW_dot a|; the equivalent lower-derivative raised-field form would carry the opposite sign
W_A W_B contains lambda_A D barlambda_B plus lambda_B D barlambda_A before contraction with symmetric f_AB

d4x_L=-i d4x_E follows from the ordered time contour, while epsilon_E^1234=+1 is an independently fixed tensor orientation
constant f_AB is symmetric and invariant; Re f is positive; the absorbed-coupling connection is exactly partial_M-i A_M
kappa_L=2i and kappa_E=-2; u_R=4/kappa_R and rho_R=4/kappa_R^2; kappa_R u_R=4 and kappa_R^2 rho_R=4
U_R=tildePhi_R E_R is a chiral-frame dual row; hat-tilde-W=E_R^(-1) tildeW E_R is the corresponding transported antichiral field strength; the bottom row connection is partial_M X+i X A_M

equations 3A.74 through 3A.81 use only covariant derivative algebra, chirality, curvature commutators, graded Leibniz rules, component projections, and gauge-covariant integration by parts
